title: Generic Containers
hints: A class template is written once with `T` and the compiler makes `Stack<int>` and `Stack<std::string>` from it when you use them (lesson 9.01). Member functions are written inside the class, so there is no `.cpp` file to worry about.
A simple `Queue<T>` can use a `std::vector<T>` and an index of the front element: `pop` moves the index forward, and when the index passes half the vector, erase the used part.
requirements: `pop`, `top` and `front` on an empty container throw `std::out_of_range`
Tests in `main` with `int` and `std::string`, including catching the exception
stretch: Constrain `T` with a concept (`std::copyable`), and a `Queue` that reuses its space as a ring.
